Python zip() pairs items from iterables by position and returns an iterator of tuples. For example, list(zip([1, 2], ['a', 'b'])) returns [(1, 'a'), (2, 'b')]. By default it stops at the shortest iterable; strict=True raises ValueError for unequal lengths in Python 3.10 or later.
